note: Questions from the CBSE Class X Science board exam 2023, Q.P. code 31/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Questions that need a figure or a drawing are left out (Q1, Q2, Q7, Q15, Q16, Q25(a), Q30, Q32). Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
MnO₂ + x HCl → MnCl₂ + y H₂O + z Cl₂
In order to balance the above chemical equation, the values of x, y and z respectively are :
questions.solution: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂. Check: 4 H, 4 Cl and 2 O on each side.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The table below has information regarding pH and the nature (acidic/basic) of four different solutions. Which one of the options in the table is correct ?
(a) Lemon juice : orange pH paper : pH 3 : basic
(b) Milk of magnesia : blue : pH 10 : basic
(c) Gastric juice : red : pH 6 : acidic
(d) Pure water : yellow : pH 7 : neutral
questions.solution: Milk of magnesia is basic with pH about 10, turning pH paper blue. Lemon juice is acidic, gastric juice has a pH of about 1 to 2, and pure water turns pH paper green, not yellow.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A metal 'X' is used in thermite process. When X is burnt in air it gives an amphoteric oxide 'Y'. 'X' and 'Y' are respectively :
questions.solution: Aluminium is the reducing metal in the thermite process, and it burns to form aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃, which is amphoteric.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Select washing soda from the following :
questions.solution: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. NaHCO₃ is baking soda.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An organism which breaks down the food material outside the body and then absorbs it is
questions.solution: Fungi such as Rhizopus (bread mould) secrete enzymes onto the food, digest it outside the body and then absorb it (saprophytic nutrition).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Consider the following statements about small intestine and select the one which is NOT correct :
options: The length of the small intestine in animals differs as it depends on the type of food they eat.
The small intestine is the site of complete digestion of food.
The small intestine receives secretions from liver and pancreas.
The villi of the small intestine absorb water from the unabsorbed food before it gets removed from the body via the anus.
questions.solution: Water is absorbed from the unabsorbed food in the large intestine, not by the villi of the small intestine. The other statements are true.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The statement that correctly describes the characteristic(s) of a gene is :
options: In individuals of a given species, a specific gene is located on a particular chromosome.
A gene is not the information source for making proteins in the cell.
Each chromosome has only one gene located all along its length.
All the inherited traits in human beings are not controlled by genes.
questions.solution: In a species, each gene has a fixed place on a particular chromosome. Genes do carry the information for making proteins, a chromosome carries many genes, and inherited traits are controlled by genes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Select from the following the correct statement about tropic movement in plants :
options: It is due to stimulus of touch and temperature.
It does not depend upon the direction of stimulus received.
It is observed only in roots and not in stems.
It is a growth related movement.
questions.solution: Tropic movements are slow growth movements directed by the stimulus (light, gravity, water, chemicals); they occur in both roots and shoots.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Select the INCORRECT match (between the plant and its vegetative part) from the following :
questions.solution: Rose is propagated by stem cuttings, not by roots. The other pairs are correct (Bryophyllum by leaf buds, potato by stem tubers, money plant by stem cuttings).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: If four identical resistors, of resistance 8 ohm, are first connected in series so as to give an effective resistance Rs, and then connected in parallel so as to give an effective resistance Rp, then the ratio Rs/Rp is
questions.solution: Rs = 4 × 8 = 32 Ω and Rp = 8/4 = 2 Ω, so Rs/Rp = 16.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In domestic electric circuits the wiring with 15 A current rating is for the electric devices which have
options: higher power ratings such as geyser.
lower power ratings such as fan.
metallic bodies and low power ratings.
non-metallic bodies and low power ratings.
questions.solution: The 15 A power circuit is used for high-power appliances such as geysers, heaters and air conditioners; the 5 A circuit is for fans and bulbs.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The colour of aqueous solution of copper sulphate turns colourless when a piece of lead is added to it.
Reason (R): Lead is more reactive than copper, and hence displaces copper from its salt solution.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: Lead is above copper in the reactivity series, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate; the blue colour fades as copper is removed from the solution. R explains A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Genes inherited from the parents decide the sex of a child.
Reason (R): X chromosome in a male child is inherited from his father.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: The sex of a child is decided by the sex chromosomes inherited from the parents, so A is true. A boy gets his X chromosome from his mother and his Y from his father, so R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Blood clotting prevents excessive loss of blood.
Reason (R): Blood clotting is due to blood plasma and white blood cells present in the blood.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: Clotting seals a cut and prevents blood loss, so A is true. Clotting is brought about by platelets, not white blood cells, so R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The strength of the magnetic field produced at the centre of a current carrying circular coil increases on increasing the number of turns in it.
Reason (R): The current in each circular turn has the same direction and the magnetic field due to each turn then just adds up.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: With n turns carrying current in the same direction, the fields of all the turns add up, so the field at the centre is n times that of one turn. R explains A.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) A compound 'X' which is prepared from gypsum has the property of hardening when mixed with proper quantity of water. Identify 'X' and write its chemical formula.
(ii) State the difference in chemical composition between baking soda and baking powder.
questions.solution: (i) X is Plaster of Paris, calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O. (ii) Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃) alone; baking powder is a mixture of baking soda and a mild edible acid such as tartaric acid.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Write balanced chemical equation for the reaction that occurs when : (i) blue coloured copper sulphate crystals are heated and (ii) Sodium hydrogen carbonate is heated during cooking.
questions.solution: (i) CuSO₄·5H₂O → CuSO₄ + 5H₂O (on heating; blue crystals turn white as they lose water of crystallisation). (ii) 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Write the role of insulin in regulating blood sugar levels in human body. Mention the disease caused due to it.
(b) How is the timing and the amount of release of insulin in the blood regulated ?
questions.solution: (a) Insulin, secreted by the pancreas, lowers the blood sugar level by helping cells take up glucose (and store it as glycogen). If it is not secreted in proper amounts, blood sugar rises, causing diabetes. (b) By a feedback mechanism: when blood sugar rises, cells of the pancreas detect it and secrete more insulin; as the sugar level falls, insulin secretion is reduced.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Name the type of blood (oxygenated / deoxygenated) transported by each of the following mentioning the path (i.e. from one organ (which place) to another (which place)). (i) Vena cava (ii) Pulmonary artery
questions.solution: (i) Vena cava: deoxygenated blood from the body organs to the right atrium of the heart. (ii) Pulmonary artery: deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: With the help of a schematic flow chart, show the breakdown of glucose in a cell to provide energy – (i) in the presence of oxygen (ii) in lack of oxygen
questions.solution: In both cases: Glucose (6 carbon) → in the cytoplasm → Pyruvate (3 carbon) + energy. (i) With oxygen: Pyruvate → in the mitochondria → Carbon dioxide + Water + a lot of energy. (ii) Lack of oxygen (in muscle cells): Pyruvate → Lactic acid (3 carbon) + energy. (In yeast without oxygen: Pyruvate → Ethanol + Carbon dioxide + energy.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Name the part of the human excretory system where nephrons are found. Write the structure and function of nephrons.
questions.solution: Nephrons are found in the kidneys. Structure: each nephron has a cup-shaped Bowman's capsule holding a cluster of capillaries (the glomerulus), followed by a long coiled tubule that joins a collecting duct. Function: blood is filtered in the glomerulus; useful substances such as glucose, amino acids, salts and much of the water are reabsorbed in the tubule, and the rest forms urine.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text:
It is observed that the power of an eye to see nearby objects as well as far off objects diminishes with age.
(i) Give reason for the above statement.
(ii) Name the defect that is likely to arise in the eyes in such a condition.
(iii) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the type of corrective lens used for restoring the vision of such an eye.
questions.solution: (i) With age the ciliary muscles weaken and the eye lens loses flexibility, so the power of accommodation decreases. (ii) Presbyopia. (iii) A bifocal lens: the upper part is a concave lens for distant vision and the lower part a convex lens for near vision (shown in the diagram).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How do harmful chemicals get accumulated progressively at each trophic level in a food chain ?
questions.solution: Pesticides and other harmful chemicals wash into soil and water and are taken up by plants. They are non-biodegradable, so they are neither broken down nor excreted and build up in the body. Each animal at the next level eats many organisms of the level below, so the concentration rises at every step. This is called biological magnification.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Identify the reducing agent in the following reactions : (i) 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O (ii) H₂O + F₂ → HF + HOF (iii) Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ (iv) 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
(b) Define a redox reaction in terms of gain or loss of oxygen.
questions.solution: (a) (i) NH₃ (ii) H₂O (iii) CO (iv) H₂. (b) A redox reaction is one in which one substance gains oxygen (is oxidised) while another loses oxygen (is reduced) at the same time.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Suggest one remedial measure each to counteract the change in pH in human beings in following cases : (i) Production of too much acid in stomach during indigestion (ii) Stung by a honey bee / nettle leaves
(b) Fresh milk has a pH of 6. When it changes into curd will its pH increase or decrease ? Why ?
questions.solution: (a) (i) Take an antacid (a mild base) such as milk of magnesia, Mg(OH)₂, to neutralise the excess acid. (ii) Rub a mild base such as baking soda on the bee sting; for a nettle sting, rub the leaf of the dock plant. (b) The pH decreases, because lactic acid forms as milk turns to curd, making it more acidic.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) State the role of ATP in cellular respiration.
(ii) What ensures sufficient exchange of gases in plants ?
(iii) State the conditions on which the direction of diffusion of gases in plant depend upon.
questions.solution: (i) ATP is the energy currency of the cell: the energy released in respiration is stored in ATP and later used to drive other cell activities. (ii) Large intercellular spaces ensure all cells are in contact with air; gases enter and leave through stomata in leaves (and lenticels in stems). (iii) It depends on the environmental conditions and the plant's needs: at night, with no photosynthesis, CO₂ is given out; in the day, CO₂ produced in respiration is used for photosynthesis and oxygen is given out.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) What is the internal energy reserve in plants and animals ?
(ii) How desert plants perform photosynthesis if their stomata remain closed during the day ?
questions.solution: (i) Plants store energy as starch and animals as glycogen. (ii) Desert plants open their stomata at night, take in CO₂ and store it as an intermediate (an acid). During the day, with stomata closed, chlorophyll absorbs light energy and the stored CO₂ is released and used to make carbohydrates.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: Give reasons for the following : (a) Danger signals installed at airports and at the top of tall buildings are of red colour. (b) The sky appears dark to the passengers flying at very high altitudes. (c) The path of a beam of light passing through a colloidal solution is visible.
questions.solution: (a) Red light has the longest wavelength and is scattered least by fog, smoke and air particles, so it can be seen from far away. (b) At very high altitudes there is almost no air or particles to scatter sunlight, so the sky looks dark. (c) The colloidal particles are large enough to scatter light, so the beam's path becomes visible (the Tyndall effect).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Why does a kitchen garden called an artificial ecosystem while a forest is considered to be a natural ecosystem ?
(ii) While designing an artificial ecosystem at home, write any two things to be kept in mind to convert it into a self-sustaining system. Give reason to justify your answer.
questions.solution: (i) A kitchen garden is made and maintained by people, who choose the plants and look after them; a forest develops and sustains itself naturally without human help. (ii) For example, in an aquarium: include producers (aquatic plants), consumers and decomposers in a balanced way, so food and oxygen are produced and wastes recycled; and provide enough light (and air), because the producers need sunlight to make food, which is the energy source for the whole system.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Construct a food chain of four trophic levels comprising the following : Hawk, snake, plants, rat.
(ii) 20,000 J of energy was transferred by the producers to the organism of second trophic level. Calculate the amount of energy that will be transferred by organisms of the third trophic level to the organisms of the fourth trophic level.
questions.solution: (i) Plants → Rat → Snake → Hawk. (ii) By the 10% law, the second level (rat) passes 10% of 20,000 J = 2,000 J to the third level (snake), which passes 10% of 2,000 J = 200 J to the fourth level (hawk).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
A saturated organic compound 'A' belongs to the homologous series of alcohols. On heating 'A' with concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K, it forms an unsaturated compound 'B' with molecular mass 28 u. The compound 'B' on addition of one mole of hydrogen in the presence of Nickel, changes to a saturated hydrocarbon 'C'.
(i) Identify A, B and C.
(ii) Write the chemical equations showing the conversion of A into B.
(iii) What happens when compound C undergoes combustion ?
(iv) State one industrial application of hydrogenation reaction.
(v) Name the products formed when compound A reacts with sodium.
questions.solution: (i) A = ethanol (C₂H₅OH), B = ethene (C₂H₄, 28 u), C = ethane (C₂H₆). (ii) CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (hot concentrated H₂SO₄, 443 K). (iii) It burns in air to give carbon dioxide and water with a lot of heat and light: 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O. (iv) Hydrogenation of vegetable oils with a nickel catalyst to make vanaspati ghee. (v) Sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) With the help of diagram, show the formation of micelles, when soap is applied on oily dirt.
(ii) Take two test tubes X and Y with 10 mL of hard water in each. In test tube 'X', add few drops of soap solution and in test tube 'Y' add a few drops of detergent solution. Shake both the test tubes for the same period. (1) In which test tube the formation of foam will be more ? Why ? (2) In which test tube is a curdy solid formed ? Why ?
questions.solution: (i) A soap molecule has an ionic (water-loving) end and a long hydrocarbon (oil-loving) tail. In water, the tails dissolve in the oily dirt and the ionic ends face the water, forming clusters called micelles with the oil trapped in the centre; the micelles are washed away by water (the diagram shows this cluster). (ii) (1) Test tube Y: detergents do not form insoluble compounds with the calcium and magnesium ions in hard water, so they lather well. (2) Test tube X: soap reacts with the calcium and magnesium salts in hard water to form an insoluble curdy precipitate (scum).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) Name the parts of a bisexual flower that are not directly involved in reproduction.
(b) Differentiate between self pollination and cross pollination. List any two significance of pollination.
(c) What is the fate of ovules and ovary after fertilization in a flower ?
questions.solution: (a) Sepals and petals. (b) Self-pollination: pollen is transferred from the anther to the stigma of the same flower (or another flower on the same plant). Cross-pollination: pollen is transferred to the stigma of a flower on another plant of the same species, by agents such as wind, water or animals. Significance: it brings the male germ cells to the female part so fertilisation can happen; cross-pollination also produces variation. (c) The ovules develop into seeds and the ovary develops into the fruit.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(a) An electric iron consumes energy at a rate of 880 W when heating is at the maximum rate and 330 W when the heating is at the minimum. If the source voltage is 220 V, calculate the current and resistance in each case.
(b) What is heating effect of electric current ?
(c) Find an expression for the amount of heat produced when a current passes through a resistor for some time.
questions.solution: (a) Maximum: I = P/V = 880 ÷ 220 = 4 A and R = V/I = 220 ÷ 4 = 55 Ω. Minimum: I = 330 ÷ 220 = 1.5 A and R = 220 ÷ 1.5 ≈ 146.7 Ω. (b) When current flows through a resistor, part of the electrical energy is converted into heat; this is the heating effect of current. (c) Work done in moving charge Q through potential difference V is W = VQ = VIt. This appears as heat, so H = VIt, and since V = IR, H = I²Rt.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Almost all metals combine with oxygen to form metal oxides. Metal oxides are generally basic in nature. But some metal oxides show both basic as well as acidic behaviour. Different metals show different reactivities towards oxygen. Some react vigorously while some do not react at all.

What happens when copper is heated in air ? (Give the equation of the reaction involved).
questions.solution: Its surface gets coated with black copper(II) oxide: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Almost all metals combine with oxygen to form metal oxides. Metal oxides are generally basic in nature. But some metal oxides show both basic as well as acidic behaviour.

Why are some metal oxides categorized as amphoteric ? Give one example.
questions.solution: Because they react with both acids and bases to form salt and water. Example: aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) or zinc oxide (ZnO).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Almost all metals combine with oxygen to form metal oxides. Metal oxides are generally basic in nature. But some metal oxides show both basic as well as acidic behaviour.

Complete the following equations : (i) Na₂O(s) + H₂O(l) → (ii) Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH →
questions.solution: (i) Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH. (ii) Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O (sodium aluminate).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Different elements show different reactivities towards oxygen.

On burning Sulphur in oxygen a colourless gas is produced. (i) Write chemical equation for the reaction. (ii) Name the gas formed. (iii) State the nature of the gas. (iv) What will be the action of this on a dry litmus paper ?
questions.solution: (i) S + O₂ → SO₂. (ii) Sulphur dioxide. (iii) It is acidic (a non-metal oxide). (iv) No effect on dry litmus paper; it turns moist blue litmus red only in the presence of water.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In order to trace the inheritance of traits Mendel crossed pea plants having one contrasting character or a pair of contrasting characters. When he crossed pea plants having round and yellow seeds with pea plants having wrinkled and green seeds, he observed that no plants with wrinkled and green seeds were obtained in the F₁ generation. When the F₁ generation pea plants were cross-bred by self-pollination, the F₂ generation had seeds with different combinations of shape and colour also.

Write any two pairs of contrasting characteristics of pea plant used by Mendel other than those mentioned above.
questions.solution: Any two of: tall and short stem; violet and white flowers; axial and terminal flower position; inflated and constricted pods; green and yellow pods.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In order to trace the inheritance of traits Mendel crossed pea plants having one contrasting character or a pair of contrasting characters.

Differentiate between dominant and recessive traits.
questions.solution: A dominant trait is expressed even when only one copy of its gene is present (in a hybrid); a recessive trait is expressed only when both copies of the gene are recessive.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
When Mendel crossed pea plants having round and yellow seeds with pea plants having wrinkled and green seeds, he observed that no plants with wrinkled and green seeds were obtained in the F₁ generation. When the F₁ generation pea plants were cross-bred by self-pollination, the F₂ generation had seeds with different combinations of shape and colour also.

State the ratio of the combinations observed in the seeds of F₂ generation (in the above case). What do you interpret from this result ?
questions.solution: 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green. Interpretation: seed shape and seed colour are inherited independently of each other, so new combinations appear in F₂.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
In order to trace the inheritance of traits Mendel crossed pea plants having one contrasting character.

Given below is a cross between a pure violet flowered pea plant (VV) and a pure white flowered pea plant (vv). Diagrammatically explain what type of progeny is obtained in F₁ generation and F₂ generation.
questions.solution: Gametes V and v give F₁: all Vv, all violet. Selfing F₁ (Vv × Vv) gives F₂: VV, Vv, Vv, vv, i.e. genotypes 1 : 2 : 1 and phenotypes 3 violet : 1 white.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Hold a concave mirror in your hand and direct its reflecting surface towards the sun. Direct the light reflected by the mirror on to a white card-board held close to the mirror. Move the card-board back and forth gradually until you find a bright, sharp spot of light on the board. This spot of light is the image of the sun on the sheet of paper; which is also termed as "Principal Focus" of the concave mirror.

List two applications of concave mirror.
questions.solution: Any two: reflectors in torches and vehicle headlights, shaving mirrors, dentists' mirrors, solar furnaces.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
A concave mirror directed towards the sun forms a bright, sharp spot of light, which is its "Principal Focus".

If the distance between the mirror and the principal focus is 15 cm, find the radius of curvature of the mirror.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
A concave mirror directed towards the sun forms a bright, sharp spot of light, which is its "Principal Focus".

Draw a ray diagram to show the type of image formed when an object is placed between pole and focus of a concave mirror.
questions.solution: A ray parallel to the axis reflects through F, and a ray along the line from the centre of curvature C reflects back on itself; the reflected rays diverge and appear to meet behind the mirror. The image is virtual, erect and magnified, behind the mirror.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An object 10 cm in size is placed at 100 cm in front of a concave mirror. If its image is formed at the same point where the object is located, find : (i) focal length of the mirror, and (ii) magnification of the image formed with sign as per Cartesian sign convention.
questions.solution: The image forms at the object only when the object is at the centre of curvature, so R = 100 cm. (i) f = R/2 = 50 cm, i.e. f = −50 cm by sign convention. (ii) m = −v/u = −(−100)/(−100) = −1: the image is real, inverted and the same size (10 cm).
